_placedBy: Four states, not a boolean. 'agent' = a scheduled run placed the order itself, from its own analysis, with nobody asking. 'directed' = an agent placed it because a human asked for it in the moment - machine-executed, human-initiated. 'assisted' = a human executed it with the agent advising - human-executed, machine-informed. 'hand' = a human acting alone. ONLY 'agent' counts toward autonomy. The brokerage reports placed_agent='agentic' for both 'agent' and 'directed' and cannot distinguish them, because the difference is who decided rather than who pressed the button - so the retro must establish whether a published specification and a scheduled run stand behind the order, and file it 'directed' when they do not. Reading the broker's flag alone would count a trade the operator asked for as evidence the system runs unattended, which is the claim the whole board rests on.

_forced: The 2026-08-05 daily entry mandate obliges the open run to publish a specification every trading day and to mark it 'forced' when a checklist item failed, so that patience and compulsion are measured apart instead of averaged together. A closed trade joins an arm only by way of the specification it came from. All three trades on the board came from no specification at all, so all three sit outside both arms and the arms are empty - which is the honest reading, not a missing number. The reason has now been different on each of four days, and the differences are the useful part: on 8/5 nothing had been published, on 8/6 the first specification published under the mandate went unexecuted and expired, on 8/7 the mandate went undischarged because the open slot fired 143 minutes late and stopped at the staleness guard, and on 8/10 the mandate was discharged, the specification again went unexecuted and expired, and the position the account actually holds came from no specification at all, and on 8/11 the reason repeats 8/7's for the first time - the open slot fired 247 minutes late, the staleness guard bound, and nothing was published under the mandate at all. On 8/12 the reason is new and is the worst of the five: no run fired inside ANY slot of the session, so the open slot did not merely miss its window, it produced nothing until 23:39 ET when it fired 846 minutes late and correctly declined at the guard. The mandate was committed 2026-08-05 11:34 ET, after that day's open run had already fired, so its first binding open slot was 2026-08-06. AS OF 2026-09-02 THE ARMS ARE STILL EMPTY AND THE REASON IS NOW STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN CIRCUMSTANTIAL: the mandate has been discharged on almost every session since, specifications have been published and marked, and not one of them has become a closed trade - they have expired unexecuted or been killed. An arm counts CLOSED TRADES attributed through the specification they came from, so a specification that never fills contributes to neither arm no matter how it was labelled. Today's MDT entry was published not-forced, correctly labelled, and expired unexecuted at 15:30, so it joins neither. The arms will stay at zero for as long as the delivery leg rather than the reasoning is the binding constraint, and that is the honest reading of the number rather than a gap in it.

Six rows reading CONFIRMED can be misread as six live hours when four and a half of them were not. A distinct 'confirmed - out of reach' state would fix that, and it is a rulebook change, so it is recommended to the operator rather than adopted here.

THE OPEN PROCESS QUESTION THE 14:22, 15:22 AND 15:35 RUNS ALL HANDED TO THIS RETRO IS WHETHER AN HOUR IS THE RIGHT DROUGHT LENGTH. IT IS ANSWERED NO, AND NOT ON TODAY'S P/L. The recommendation for the operator, not an agent-made rule change: an away-side kill should be conditioned on the thing it claims to detect - the setup leaving the tape - rather than on a bare print drought, or it should be dropped and the 15:30 expiry left to do the work it was widened to do.

That refusal cost a visible and rising number all afternoon and was made anyway, which is what a pre-registered test is for. THE ONE THING THE DAY ARGUES AGAINST IS THE TRIGGER, NOT THE HONOURING OF IT, and three separate runs said so unprompted: 'the prior session low' on a shelf whose floor is being probed may be too tight a test, and the place to fix that is the NEXT entry's invalidation list, written before the fact. That is the correct location for the fix and this retro endorses none of it into the rulebook, because writing a rule is the operator's act and not a read-only run's. PRICED AGAINST THE BELL WITHOUT EDITORIALISING THE DIRECTION: MDT closed its regular session at 93.110, so the kill cost 7.92 on four shares on the runs' own 91.13 basis and 4.40 on the specification's 92.01 limit, +0.783% and +0.435% of the account respectively. THE 2026-08-18 CONSTRAINT THAT WIDENING THE TIME IS NOT PERMISSION TO WIDEN THE PRICE WAS TESTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AND HELD IN BOTH, repeatedly and at a cost that was visible while it was being paid. The limit was not RAISED at 11:21, 12:21, 13:21, 14:21 or 15:21 as the gap to the offer ran 0.37, 0.49, 0.73, 0.65 and 0.53; it was not LOWERED to 91.13 at 10:21 when the withdrawing run noted the specification had become CHEAPER than its own limit; and it was not carried into tomorrow by the pre-close. That is the drift policy working rather than being audited. WHAT TRIPS IS THE THIRD CONSTRAINT ATTACHED TO THE SAME 2026-08-18 CHANGE, AND IT IS WORSE THAN LAST NIGHT'S IN TWO WAYS. That change bought a five-and-a-half-hour execution window with three constraints attached, and the one requiring the publishing run to notify the operator went unlogged AGAIN - second consecutive session, third of the last four. FIRST, IT IS NO LONGER A REGRESSION BUT A RATE: the constraint has now been honoured on one of the last four sessions that published a specification, which means the operative rule is closer to 'sometimes' than to what the operator agreed to. SECOND, IT EXTENDED TO THE KILL, which the record has never had to note before - a live instruction was withdrawn with no notification logged, so the delivery leg failed at both ends of the same specification's short life. IT DOES NOT FOLLOW A WIN - the account is flat, has been since 8/14, and the last closed trade was OKLO at -0.72. It is not tilt; it is erosion, which is the failure mode the drift policy names in its own first sentence. A loosening whose attached constraint lapses is a larger loosening than the one that was agreed to, and it lapses without a decision, a date or a diff. NO REMEDY IS PROPOSED HERE beyond recording it and notifying: the constraint already exists in writing, it does not need a new rule, and inventing one would itself be the agent changing the rulebook. A SECOND LIMB IS NOTED AND IT IS AN IMPROVEMENT RATHER THAN A TRIP, recorded because the 9/1 ledger raised it and a finding that is only ever reported when it worsens is not a finding. That night the graded corpus had shrunk sevenfold because six hourlies wrote their reasoning into runs.json instead of why.json; today six of the seven trading runs wrote did entries and only the 12:21 hourly did not. The corpus this retro could grade is six entries rather than one. The underlying question - whether an hourly confirmation owes a did entry - is still the operator's and is still open.

THE MEASUREMENT LIMB, EIGHTH CONSECUTIVE NIGHT, AND TONIGHT IT IS SMALL IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. That runs in the direction that flatters this board's own decision, which is the direction to be slowest about, and it is the fifteenth consecutive session on which a pre-bell figure has stood in for a close. FINDING TWO, FOR THE BOARD: the 11:21 run's estimate that the kill's cost window shut around 11:05 ET is four minutes early against a minute series - the true last marketable minute is 15:09Z, 11:09 ET - which is a ten-minute-bar granularity artefact that the run itself hedged with 'roughly'. A recomputation that confirms a run is worth publishing as loudly as one that does not. ACROSS EIGHT NIGHTS THE ERRORS HAVE STILL RUN BOTH WAYS, which continues to support the plainer reading that figures are handled loosely rather than tilted. What is new tonight is that the loose figure has a mechanism rather than a magnitude: the pre-bell substitution's error is not drift, it is the closing auction, and no quote taken before 16:00 can contain it. That is a stronger version of the 8/20 conclusion than eight sessions of scattered magnitudes were, and the conclusion is unchanged and still unadopted - it is the operator's call whether the pre-close should stop pricing against a pre-bell bid at all.
